course.title: Atomic – Cambridge Lower Secondary Mathematics — Stage 9

unit.title: Volume, surface area and symmetry
unit.blurb: Volume of prisms and cylinders, surface area of triangular prisms, pyramids and cylinders, and planes of symmetry in 3D shapes.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Use V = area of cross-section × length to find the volume of prisms and cylinders, and solve problems.

O2.t: Find the surface area of triangular prisms, pyramids and cylinders, using nets.

O3.t: Identify planes of symmetry in 3D shapes.

p: A **prism** has the same cross-section all the way through. **Volume = area of cross-section × length**.
A **cylinder** is a prism with a circular cross-section: **V = πr²h**.

lesson.q: A triangular prism has a triangle of base 8 cm and height 5 cm, and length 12 cm. Find its volume.

p: 1 cm³ = 1 ml and 1000 cm³ = 1 litre. 1 m³ = 1 000 000 cm³.
V = πr²h: square the radius BEFORE multiplying by π and h. Using the diameter instead of the radius gives 4 times the volume.

p: The **surface area** is the total area of all the faces. Sketch the **net** and add up each face.
Triangular prism: 2 triangles + 3 rectangles. Pyramid: base + triangular faces.

lesson.q: A square-based pyramid has base 6 cm and triangle faces of height 5 cm. Find its surface area.

p: A cylinder opens into **two circles** and a **rectangle** whose length is the circumference 2πr. **Surface area = 2πr² + 2πrh**.
The rectangle's width is the CIRCUMFERENCE (2πr), not the radius.

p: A **plane of symmetry** cuts a solid into two halves that are mirror images.
A cuboid (not a cube) has **3** planes of symmetry. A cube has **9**. A square-based pyramid has **4**. A cylinder has **infinitely many**.
A cube has diagonal planes too (through opposite edges): 3 parallel to the faces + 6 diagonal = 9.
